questions.question:
When you render `

{text}

` where `text` contains ``, what happens?
options: React escapes it and renders the literal text on the page, not executable HTML
The component silently fails to render
questions.explanation: JSX interpolation like {text} is escaped by default, which is exactly why most XSS discussion in React centers on the APIs that bypass this.

questions.question: What does `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` do differently from normal JSX interpolation?
options: It bypasses React's automatic escaping and injects raw HTML directly, which is unsafe for unsanitized user input
It only works with trusted internal content and errors on user input
It is identical to normal JSX interpolation, just named differently
questions.explanation: The deliberately alarming name signals that this prop opts out of React's default escaping — any unsanitized HTML passed to it executes as-is.

questions.question: Why does manually setting `ref.current.innerHTML = message` in a useEffect carry the same risk as `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`?
options: It doesn't — refs are always safe
React's escaping protections only apply to content it renders itself, not to direct DOM mutations performed via refs
Refs are deprecated and should never be used
It only matters in class components
questions.explanation: Both bypass React's rendering pipeline and inject raw HTML into the DOM directly, carrying identical XSS risk if the content is unsanitized user input.

questions.question: What does `npm audit` help protect against?
options: Known vulnerabilities in your project's dependency tree, including transitive dependencies
questions.explanation: npm audit scans installed packages against known vulnerability databases, surfacing supply-chain risk that doesn't come from your own application code.
